text:
Seven straight losses, the last a 6-3 defeat in Chicago that The Leafs Nation called rock bottom, and a 1-9-0 record over the last ten games. On Monday, before that loss, new GM John Chayka publicly backed first-year coach Jim Hiller, calling the results unacceptable, per The Canadian Press. When a GM has to say that in November, you know where things stand.

The uncomfortable part is that the losing is earned. During the streak Toronto has had 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they've been outscored 29-12. For the season the Leafs sit at 46%, and our expected points say they've been slightly unlucky, not robbed. Sergei Bobrovsky has made it worse: 0-5-0 with an .827 save percentage over his last five starts, 7.6 goals worse than expected. William Nylander has four points in his last ten games against 10.1 expected, and his effort has become a talk-show topic.

The one thing working is Auston Matthews. His line with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan has outscored opponents 10-4 at 54% of the expected goals. Gavin McKenna's rookie season is the other reason to watch. Morgan Rielly was slated to return Tuesday. Our playoff odds are 3%, which tells you how deep the hole already is.
